data.title: Draft a weekly update from existing tools
data.summary: Reuse a team template and reconcile shipped work, metrics and blockers across authorized sources.

facts.text: Anthropic’s Cowork guide demonstrates drafting a recurring engineering update from an existing template, a metrics CSV, Asana and Slack.

prerequisites: Access to Claude Cowork with existing team sources; check account, client and workspace availability.
The existing weekly update format and reporting cutoff.
steps: Find the existing weekly report and template; define the time window and timezone.
Collect completed items, metrics and blockers from the approved source set. Record unavailable sources.
Deduplicate repeated updates and distinguish shipped items from planned work.
Reconcile each metric to the CSV and cite the source for each blocker or commitment.
Save a draft for review. Reuse an existing schedule only after a manual pilot succeeds.
data.output: a source-linked weekly update draft and unresolved-source list
validation: Show the discrepancy and the later evidence.
Mark partial coverage; do not invent a complete weekly report.
limitations: Sintra-authored procedure based on provider documentation or demonstrations; no execution in the named app was performed.
Availability and results depend on your inputs, enabled tools and permissions; a suggested practice result is not a measured outcome.
data.prompt: Use [existing template] for the week ending [date/timezone]. Gather shipped work from [authorized board], metrics from [CSV] and blockers from [channel/time range]. Reuse the current report rather than create a competing one. Cite each material claim, reconcile metrics and distinguish completed code from a completed rollout. List unavailable sources, conflicts and unknown owners. Save a draft and source receipt for review; do not post it or create a schedule.
tips: Use the cutoff consistently across messages and exports.
Keep draft preparation separate from publishing to a channel.
